The sources agree on the core limits, though some third-party pages disagree on egress and file storage. The official Supabase pricing page is the most authoritative, and it lists 5 GB cached egress, 1 GB file storage, and a note that free projects are paused after 1 week of inactivity. It also caps accounts at 2 active projects.

Other summaries give the same database and user figures. One reports a 500 MB database limit, 50,000 monthly active users, and 5 GB of egress, with file storage at 500 MB. A costbench page instead lists egress at 500 MB/month, which conflicts with the official figure. Treat that page as unreliable on this point.

On the pause, one source describes the effect: a paused project keeps its data, but the app goes dark until someone manually restores it from the dashboard.

Upgrading to Pro removes the pause. A Pro-plan summary says it has increased resource limits and removes the inactivity pause. The official Pro tier lists 8 GB disk size per project (then $0.125 per GB) and 250 GB egress (then $0.09 per GB).

Bottom line: the free tier is 500 MB database per project, 2 active projects, a 1-week inactivity pause, and roughly 5 GB cached egress and 1 GB file storage per the official page. I did not verify the exact database-size and egress wording on Supabase's own docs beyond the pricing page.

Neon's official docs and FAQ agree on the core Free plan limits, but sources conflict on a few details.

**Free plan (official docs and FAQ):** Each project gets 100 CU-hours of compute and 0.5 GB of storage per month, with up to 10 branches per project. Compute scales to zero after 5 minutes idle and can scale up to 2 CU. The plan costs $0/month, and hitting a monthly limit suspends compute until the next billing cycle. (Sources: neon.com/faqs/free-plan-limits-and-quotas, neon.com/pricing, neon.com/faqs/managed-postgres-databases-free-tier)

**Paid rates:** Launch is $0.106 per CU-hour, and Scale is $0.222 per CU-hour. Both are $0.35 per GB-month for storage. (Sources: neon.com/faqs/free-plan-limits-and-quotas, swyftstack.com, jetadmin.io)

**Conflicts to be aware of:**
- **Minimum fee:** The Neon pricing page says paid plans have no monthly minimum. The plans documentation says Launch and Scale have a $5 minimum monthly fee. The docs page is probably the more specific source, but I couldn't confirm which is current.
- **Older or inconsistent figures:** An Orb blog post lists a $19 Launch plan with 10 GB storage, and a 191.9 compute-hours figure for Free. A different Neon page cites 50 CU-hours per project for Free. These appear outdated or inconsistent with the current official docs, so I'd treat them with caution.

Pricing changes often, so the official plans page (neon.com/docs/introduction/plans) is the authoritative check.

PlanetScale has no free tier for Postgres, according to most of the sources I found. The main exception is CostBench, which is inconsistent with itself.

- **No free tier:** Several sources say PlanetScale removed its free Hobby plan in April 2024 and has not restored it. PlanetScale has no free tier. It removed its free Hobby plan in April 2024 and has not brought it back.
- **Cheapest paid option:** The entry point is a single-node Postgres instance (PS-5) for about $5/month. One source says the Base plan launched on October 30, 2025 for a single-node, non-HA Postgres database (the PS-5 SKU) aimed at development and non-critical workloads.
- **HA pricing:** A 3-node high-availability cluster starts around $15/month. 3-node HA clusters from $15/month
- **Conflicting source:** Some CostBench pages say a free plan exists. One claims PlanetScale offers a forever free plan as of June 2026. Other CostBench pages on the same topic say No free tier available, and its free-tier claims also conflict with its own listed tiers, so I'd discount them.
- **Alternatives with free tiers:** Neon and Supabase are the usual free Postgres options. Neon offers a free tier with 0.5 GB storage and autoscaling Postgres, and Supabase includes 500 MB free Postgres plus auth and storage.

The weight of evidence says PlanetScale Postgres has no free tier as of October 2026. Confirm on PlanetScale's pricing page before relying on it, since the CostBench figures conflict.

content.text:
**Short version:** Neon and Supabase have real free tiers. PlanetScale probably has none for Postgres. I couldn't open the vendors' pricing pages directly because every fetch failed with "proxy refused the connection". Everything below comes from search-result summaries, so please check the vendor pages before relying on any number.

| | Neon | Supabase | PlanetScale (Postgres) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free tier? | Yes, $0/month | Yes | Probably no |
| Storage | 0.5 GB per project | 500 MB database per project | n/a |
| Compute | 100 CU-hours per project per month, up to 2 CU | Not stated in the results I got | n/a |
| Idle behaviour | Scales to zero after 5 minutes idle | Project pauses after 1 week of inactivity, and you restore it manually | n/a |
| Other limits | Up to 10 branches per project. Compute suspends when you hit a monthly limit. | 2 active projects, 50,000 monthly active users, 5 GB cached egress, 1 GB file storage | n/a |
| Cheapest paid | Launch at $0.106 per CU-hour and $0.35 per GB-month of storage | Pro, with 8 GB disk and 250 GB egress | Base plan: single-node PS-5 from about $5/month. A 3-node HA cluster starts around $15/month. |

**Where each number comes from**
- **Neon:** The 100 CU-hours, 0.5 GB, 10 branches and 5-minute scale-to-zero are from [Neon's free plan FAQ](https://neon.com/faqs/free-plan-limits-and-quotas) and [Neon's pricing page](https://neon.com/pricing), as relayed by search. The paid rates are from the same FAQ and third-party posts ([swyftstack](https://swyftstack.com/blog/neon-pricing-explained), [jetadmin](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/neon-pricing/)).
- **Supabase:** The 2 projects, 1-week pause, 5 GB egress and 1 GB file storage are from the [official pricing page](https://supabase.com/pricing.md). The 500 MB database and 50,000 monthly active users come from third-party summaries, such as [Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/supabase-pricing-free-tier-limits-pro-costs-egress.md). The Pro figures (8 GB disk, 250 GB egress) are also from the pricing page.
- **PlanetScale:** The "no free tier" claim is from several third-party sources, for example [Bytebase's comparison](https://www.bytebase.com/blog/postgres-hosting-options-pricing-comparison/) and [Toolradar](https://toolradar.com/tools/planetscale/pricing). They say the free Hobby plan was removed in April 2024. The $5 and $15 prices come from the same kind of third-party pages, not from planetscale.com.

**Conflicts**
- **Neon minimum fee:** Neon's pricing page says paid plans have no monthly minimum, but the plans docs mention a $5 minimum on Launch and Scale. Some blogs also show older figures, such as 50 CU-hours or a $19 Launch plan. I treated those as outdated.
- **Supabase egress:** One third-party page says 500 MB egress, which conflicts with the official 5 GB, so I used the official figure.
- **PlanetScale free plan:** One site, [CostBench](https://costbench.com/software/database-as-service/planetscale/free-plan/), claims a free plan exists, but its own other pages say there isn't one. I discounted it.

If you tell me which of these matters most (idle behaviour, storage or price), I can retry the official pages or narrow the comparison.
